new_material_candidates.name: EVOTOOL — Self-Evolving Tool-Use Policy Optimization
new_material_candidates.material_reason: EVOTOOL is materially distinct from existing tool-agent candidates because it explicitly decomposes the agent policy into Planner, Selector, Caller, and Synthesizer modules and optimizes them through trajectory-grounded blame attribution, targeted natural-language mutation, and diversity-aware evolutionary selection.

reference_or_screened.name: EvolveR
reference_or_screened.relevance: Implements a closed-loop experience lifecycle with offline trajectory distillation, online retrieval of reusable principles, and policy reinforcement.
reference_or_screened.reason: An official executable repository and public manuscript were verified, but this bounded pass did not independently bind a primary archival ICML proceedings record; final claim-bearing promotion should not rely only on repository acceptance metadata.

reference_or_screened.name: MUSE — Learning on the Job
reference_or_screened.relevance: Uses hierarchical memory and post-execution experience refinement to accumulate reusable experience across long-horizon productivity tasks.
reference_or_screened.reason: The research is highly relevant, but this pass did not bind a direct primary ACL Anthology paper record strongly enough to promote it as an additional claim-bearing comparator.

n_h2_reference_research.name: EVOTOOL
n_h2_reference_research.relevance: Evolves modular tool-use policies and reports transfer across tool-use datasets and backbone models.
n_h2_reference_research.reason: The transferred object remains a tool-use agent policy; no evidence transfers the same learned decision mechanism into E2 structured ML and E3 vision.

n_h2_reference_research.name: EvolveR

n_h2_reference_research.name: MUSE
n_h2_reference_research.relevance: Accumulates hierarchical experience memory for long-horizon agent tasks.
n_h2_reference_research.reason: Experience reuse within long-horizon agents does not establish a cross-family E1-E2-E3 learned transfer mechanism.
